title: Scheduler jitter causing micro-queue bursts and tail latency spikes — remediation plan
creator: Miguel Alvarez
description: Follow-up ticket for a series of intermittent tail-latency spikes observed in the continuous batching runtime. Alerts indicated micro-queue bursts where a small subset of requests experienced 5x latency increases for short durations. This ticket consolidates investigation notes, RCA, and concrete action items to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: Between 2026-02-08 and 2026-02-09 we observed recurring 95th/99th token latency spikes across several serving clusters. Traces show many requests were enqueued into very small micro-queues and then released simultaneously due to a scheduler timer alignment issue, causing brief GPU saturation and unfair slot allocation.
impact: Intermittent increased tail latency for hosted customers on shared dedicated pools; elevated error budgets on two SLOs for a 3-hour rolling window. No data loss or correctness regressions observed. Customer support opened three tickets; two were on trial accounts causing churn risk.

root_cause_analysis: The continuous batching scheduler uses per-worker timers to flush batch windows when either a max-window or timer expiry triggers. An optimization introduced in runtime-1.21 replaced distributed random jitter with a low-entropy compaction that reduced timer variance to improve average throughput. Under certain steady-rate workloads this reduction allowed timers across worker threads to drift into micro-synchrony. When synchronization occurred, many small queues flushed simultaneously into the batch coalescer, causing temporary slot contention on the GPU and unfair prioritization of in-flight requests. Additionally, a race in the priority preemption path amplified the effect: preemption logic can starve bursty background work when a synchronized flush creates a surge of high-priority small batches.
mitigations_completed: Hotfix: reintroduced per-worker high-entropy jitter to timer expiries (gh/runtime#1297) - rolled to canary - verified reduction in simultaneous flush events
Temporary rate-smoothing gate deployed to serving plane to throttle sudden ingress bursts while longer-term fixes are validated (gh/infra#834)
Dashboard panels added to Console: micro-queue size histogram, timer alignment heatmap, and sudden-flush event counter (console-dash#42)
mitigations_pending: Rewrite scheduler compaction heuristic to account for observed workload autocorrelation instead of fixed compaction thresholds
Add fairness token-bucket fallback when preemption path detects repeated starvation for background slots
Extend tracing sampling to capture full scheduler state for 1% of requests for 48 hours in canary clusters
action_items: ENG: Implement adaptive jitter generator that seeds per-worker timers from an entropy pool and ties jitter to measured autocorrelation (owner: Priya Patel, due: 2026-03-20)
ENG: Introduce fairness fallback: if a worker detects N consecutive preemptions > threshold, temporarily raise background priority (owner: Arun Singh, due: 2026-03-15)
ENG/OBS: Add high-resolution histogram and alert that fires when >5% of workers flush within a 50ms window (owner: Elena Park, due: 2026-03-10)
SRE: Run 48-hour synthetic soak with mixed short/long sequences to validate under real traffic mixes (owner: Rowan Li, due: 2026-03-18)
PM: Prepare customer communications template and support playbook for affected accounts (owner: Sarah Kim, due: 2026-03-12)
testing_plan: Create deterministic reproducer harness using gh/benchmarks#211; run across multiple GPU instance types (A100, H100) and different sequence-length distributions. Test both merged jitter and adaptive jitter approaches with 72-hour soaks. Verify tail-latency and fairness metrics do not regress compared to pre-incident baseline.
rollback_plan: If adaptive jitter introduces regressions in throughput or avg-latency, revert to hotfixed main branch which reinstates high-entropy jitter. For canary clusters, allow automatic rollback via existing CI gate if micro-queue flush-count alert > threshold for 30 minutes.
release_plan: Merge adaptive jitter + fairness fallback into runtime-1.22.1 branch; deploy to canary (5% traffic) for 72-hour soak, then 25% for 48 hours, then full rollout with gradual traffic ramp. Coordinate Console dashboard release to match rollout window.
post_release_monitoring: Enable canary tracing capture for 1% of requests for first 7 days
SLO auto-rollback configured: if 99th token latency > 2x baseline for 60 minutes, trigger automated rollback
Weekly review of micro-queue histogram and priority-starvation counters for 4 weeks

notes: Key lesson: low-entropy optimizations that improve average throughput can create emergent synchronization under correlated workloads; instrumentation must capture timer-phase distributions
Consider adding deterministic chaos experiments to CI that attempt to align timers across workers to detect similar failure modes early
